questions.prompt: At a bridge opening too narrow for simultaneous passage, which procedure matters?
answers: The narrow-fairway meeting procedure
An automatic right to go first
Overtaking to clear the approach
questions.explanation: Article 6.24 refers to the narrow-fairway rules unless width allows simultaneous passage.

questions.prompt: A fixed bridge opening shows a red prohibition signal. What does that mean?
answers: Do not use that opening
Pass if headroom is adequate
It is only a recommendation
questions.explanation: Red or A.1 marks the prohibited opening.

questions.prompt: What must be compared with actual bridge clearance?
answers: The vessel’s full air draught at the current water level
Only its beam
Only its water draught
questions.explanation: Raised equipment and changing water level affect available headroom.

questions.prompt: What should you do on approach to a movable bridge?
answers: Reduce speed and obey bridge staff instructions
Maintain cruising speed until the span moves
Overtake waiting traffic unless a horn sounds
questions.explanation: The approach and passage are controlled by Article 6.26.

questions.prompt: A movable bridge shows red and green together. Is passage open?
answers: No; opening is being prepared
Yes; green always cancels red
Yes for small craft only
questions.explanation: The combined signal is still a no-passage state.

questions.prompt: At an ordinary weir opening, what marking normally permits passage?
answers: E.1 on both sides of the opening
One red light on either side
The absence of any sign
questions.explanation: Article 6.27 specifies E.1 on both sides, with an overhead-bridge alternative.

questions.prompt: When B.5 is displayed in a lock basin and you cannot enter immediately, where do you stop?
answers: Short of the B.5 board
Alongside the gates
Inside the chamber if space looks available
questions.explanation: Reduce speed and stop before the marked limit.

questions.prompt: When locked with larger vessels, when may a small craft enter?
answers: Only on invitation and after the other vessels
First, because it is manoeuvrable
Whenever the signal first changes
questions.explanation: Article 6.28 specifies invitation and order for small craft.

questions.prompt: Two red lock-entry lights one above the other mean what?
answers: No entry; lock out of service
Prepare for immediate entry
Exit permitted
questions.explanation: The vertical pair is the out-of-service entry state.

questions.prompt: One or two green lights at the lock exit indicate what?
answers: Exit permitted
Lock out of service
Wait for the next cycle
questions.explanation: Green is the exit permission display.

questions.prompt: Why can lock passage depart from simple order of arrival?
answers: Special priority markings and lock staff instructions
A smaller boat always goes first
AIS targets are sorted by speed
questions.explanation: Article 6.29 states special priorities and staff can direct passage.

questions.prompt: Where should a berth be chosen under the general rule?
answers: Near the bank without obstructing navigation
At the middle of the fairway
Anywhere a mooring line reaches
questions.explanation: Article 7.01 links bank proximity to draught and unobstructed traffic.

questions.prompt: May a vessel berth under a bridge because the wall is convenient?
answers: No; that is among the prohibited locations
Yes unless a red light is showing
Yes for an overnight stop only
questions.explanation: Article 7.02 prohibits berthing under bridges.

questions.prompt: What does A.6 indicate on the side where it is placed?
answers: Anchoring is prohibited
Berthing is required
Shore power is available
questions.explanation: The anchoring restriction applies to the indicated side.

questions.prompt: May a handrail or tree be used to make fast?
answers: No; use suitable permitted fittings
Yes if protected with a line sleeve
Yes whenever a berth is signed E.5
questions.explanation: Article 7.04 forbids making fast or warping from such objects.

questions.prompt: What does the breadth on E.5.1 measure?
answers: The permitted berthing width from the sign
The vessel’s air draught
The maximum lock length
questions.explanation: Article 7.05 measures the marked width from the sign.

questions.prompt: What does B.12 generally require at the marked berth?
answers: Connection to onshore power
A distress signal
An anchor watch only
questions.explanation: Article 7.06 sets the onshore-power requirement with specified exceptions.

questions.prompt: A stationary vessel lying in the fairway needs what?
answers: A continuous effective watch
No surveillance if moored
Only an AIS transmission
questions.explanation: Article 7.08 requires a watch in the fairway.

questions.prompt: The bridge mouth looks clear but two-way passing width is uncertain. What do you establish first?
answers: The applicable narrow-fairway arrangement and safe waiting point
That your engine is faster than the oncoming boat
That the other skipper can reverse
questions.explanation: Do not create a meeting where width is uncertain.

questions.prompt: One fixed opening is red and another has a recommended-opening sign. Where do you plan passage?
answers: Assess the recommended usable opening and its direction
Use the red-marked opening if shortest
Pass between the bridge piers outside all openings
questions.explanation: The red opening is prohibited; D.1 indicates a recommended route subject to direction.

questions.prompt: Your aerial raises the boat above the clearance shown for the current water level. What now?
answers: Do not commit until full clearance is established
Lower the engine speed to make the boat shorter
Use the same opening because the hull fits
questions.explanation: Air draught includes equipment above the hull.

questions.prompt: Bridge lights change from red to red with green as the span begins moving. What do you do?
answers: Remain clear; entry is still prohibited
Accelerate through before it opens fully
Follow another vessel without checking
questions.explanation: Red with green means preparation, not permission.

questions.prompt: A weir opening has no E.1 boards on both sides and no overhead-bridge authorization. What is the decision?
answers: Do not use that opening
Enter if the water appears deep
Use the next unmarked opening
questions.explanation: The normal weir permission requires E.1 on each side.

questions.prompt: You arrive at the lock basin behind a commercial vessel in your small craft. What is your plan?
answers: Wait for invitation and enter after it if locking together
Overtake inside the basin
Demand a separate lockage
questions.explanation: The small-craft and overtaking rules govern the queue.

questions.prompt: One red and one green lock-entry light are showing together. What do you do?
answers: Wait outside; the lock is being prepared
Enter because one light is green
Follow a vessel already leaving
questions.explanation: The mixed entry display is still no entry.

questions.prompt: The lock-entry signals are dark and there is no substitute board or instruction. May you enter?
answers: No; obtain an express order from lock staff
Yes if the gate is open
Yes if no vessel is visible
questions.explanation: Article 6.28 bis prohibits entry without lights/boards except by express staff order.

questions.prompt: A marked priority vessel approaches the lock after you. What should you do?
answers: Facilitate its priority passage and follow staff directions
Insist on arriving first
Enter before its bow reaches the basin
questions.explanation: Article 6.29 provides specified priority over arrival order.

questions.prompt: Your intended berth would reduce the fairway to a narrow squeeze. What is appropriate?
answers: Choose another lawful berth that leaves navigation clear
Berth and ask traffic to pass around
Deploy a fender so the protrusion is safe
questions.explanation: General and location-specific berthing rules protect the fairway.

questions.prompt: The bank bears A.7 and a handy tree stands nearby. How should you secure?
answers: Do not make fast there; seek a permitted fitting and sector
Use the tree because the prohibition concerns anchors
Use the handrail and set an anchor
questions.explanation: Article 7.04 forbids the signed side and unsuitable structures.

questions.prompt: E.5.2 shows a permitted band between two distances from the sign. Where may you berth?
answers: Within the marked band on that side
Anywhere along the riverbank
Only at the centreline of the fairway
questions.explanation: The two measured distances bound the berth.

questions.prompt: A berth has B.12 and your vessel uses ordinary generator power. What is the default expectation?
answers: Use onshore power unless a stated exception applies
Run the generator because you are small craft
Ignore B.12 if a shore cable is inconvenient
questions.explanation: Article 7.06 requires shore-power connection at B.12, subject to exceptions.

questions.prompt: A vessel marked under Article 3.14 paragraph 2 is berthed nearby. Which minimum separation normally applies?
questions.explanation: The paragraph 2 marking maps to 50 m, subject to stated exceptions.

questions.prompt: Which rule applies at a bridge opening that is not clearly wide enough for simultaneous passage?
answers: The narrow-fairway meeting procedure
Automatic priority for the smaller vessel
Overtaking permission for the faster vessel
questions.explanation: Article 6.24 applies Article 6.07 unless width is sufficient.

questions.prompt: What does a red signal at a fixed-bridge opening indicate?
answers: That opening is prohibited for navigation
That it is the recommended opening
That only small craft may enter
questions.explanation: Article 6.25 provides the red/A.1 closure marking.

questions.prompt: What does the D.1 family indicate at a fixed bridge?
answers: A recommended opening, with its direction governed by the variant
A compulsory mooring point
A closed lock chamber
questions.explanation: The specific D.1 variant and associated marking determine direction.

questions.prompt: What must be included when checking headroom?
answers: Full air draught, equipment and actual water level
Water draught only
Beam and propeller diameter only
questions.explanation: Clearance is measured against the vessel’s actual vertical profile.

questions.prompt: What should a boatmaster do on approach to a movable bridge?
answers: Reduce speed and comply with bridge staff directions
Overtake the queue to reach the span
Ignore B.5 if passage is delayed
questions.explanation: Article 6.26 governs the approach.

questions.prompt: A movable bridge shows red and green together. What is the passage state?
answers: Still prohibited while opening is prepared
Open for passage in both directions
Open only for vessels under 20 m
questions.explanation: The mixed display is preparation, not permission.

questions.prompt: What do two red lights vertically at a movable bridge mean?
answers: Opening for navigation is suspended
Bridge is ready for immediate passage
Only downstream traffic may pass
questions.explanation: Article 6.26 distinguishes vertical red from the normal closed state.

questions.prompt: What ordinarily authorizes passage through a weir opening?
answers: E.1 marking on both sides of the opening
A single red light
A sound signal alone
questions.explanation: Article 6.27 provides the E.1 rule and overhead-bridge exception.

questions.prompt: Where must a vessel stop if it cannot enter a lock immediately and B.5 is displayed?
answers: Short of the B.5 board
Immediately against the gate
Inside the chamber alongside another vessel
questions.explanation: Article 6.28 specifies the approach limit.

questions.prompt: May a small craft demand separate locking as a right?
answers: No
Yes whenever it arrived first
Yes if its engine is running
questions.explanation: The small-craft provisions prohibit a demand for separate locking.

questions.prompt: When locked with other vessels, when does a small craft enter?
answers: When invited, after those vessels
Before them, to use the free corner
As soon as any signal appears
questions.explanation: Invitation and entry order are explicit.

questions.prompt: What is the rule on overtaking in or near a lock?
answers: It is prohibited
It is required for smaller vessels
It is permitted if both vessels sound one blast
questions.explanation: Article 6.28 prohibits overtaking in or near locks.

questions.prompt: Two red lock-entry lights one above another indicate what?
answers: No entry; lock out of service
Lock being prepared for opening
Entry permitted for small craft
questions.explanation: The vertically aligned red pair marks out of service.

questions.prompt: What do one or two green lock-exit lights mean?
answers: Exit permitted
Entry prohibited but exit not addressed
Lock out of service
questions.explanation: Green permits exit under the exit-signal rule.

questions.prompt: With no lock lights or substitute boards, when may you enter?
answers: Only on express order from lock staff
Whenever the gate appears open
When the basin is empty
questions.explanation: No light/board means no entry absent express staff order.

questions.prompt: Which situation can override simple arrival order at a lock?
answers: A vessel carrying the specified priority marking
A vessel with the newest chart display
Any small craft with a short waiting time
questions.explanation: Article 6.29 identifies marked priority vessels.

questions.prompt: How should a stationary vessel be positioned under the general berthing rule?
answers: Near the bank as conditions permit without obstructing navigation
Across the fairway for better current control
Under the nearest bridge by default
questions.explanation: Article 7.01 balances bank proximity and unobstructed navigation.

questions.prompt: Is berthing under a bridge ordinarily permitted under Article 7.02?
answers: No
Yes if the bridge has green lights
Yes if the water is deep enough
questions.explanation: Under-bridge berthing is among the prohibited locations.

questions.prompt: Which sign prohibits anchoring on its side?
questions.explanation: Article 7.03 gives A.6 the anchoring prohibition.

questions.prompt: What may be used for making fast under Article 7.04?
answers: A suitable permitted fitting in an allowed sector
A handrail or tree
Any bank marker stone
questions.explanation: Trees, railings and markers are prohibited as securing points.

questions.prompt: What does a dimension on E.5.1 define?
answers: Permitted berthing width measured from the sign
Bridge headroom
Minimum distance from dangerous cargo
questions.explanation: The E.5.1 width is measured from the sign.

questions.prompt: What does B.12 require at a berthing area, subject to stated exceptions?
answers: Connection to an onshore power supply
A continuous sound signal
A compulsory anchor watch for every craft
questions.explanation: The onshore-power requirement is in Article 7.06.

questions.prompt: What is the normal minimum separation for an Article 3.14 paragraph 3 marked vessel when berthed?
questions.explanation: Article 7.07 sets the paragraph 3 distance at 100 m, with stated exceptions.

questions.prompt: What watch is required aboard a vessel lying in the fairway?
answers: A continuous efficient watch
No watch if lines are secure
Only an unattended AIS receiver
questions.explanation: Article 7.08 requires an efficient continuous watch.
